thread:
omar: Quick sync — proposing we split the enrichment service into a lightweight api layer + stateful worker pool. want to capture tradeoffs and an incremental cutover plan.
alyssa: +1. this has been a pain for scaling. curious about data migration approach.
jess: Agree. Also want clear ownership for KV cache and failure modes.
omar: Draft plan: 1) create enricher-api (stateless HTTP façade), 2) extract stateful enrichers into enricher-worker (writes to a durability store), 3) use a migration queue for existing sessions.
rachel: migration queue = which system? can we reuse the existing session-mesh stream or do a one-off backfill?
omar: Prefer using session-mesh stream for live traffic and a one-off backfill job for historical sessions. minimizes codepath divergence.
mark: Concern: latency-sensitive requests today rely on in-process enrichers and KV cache hits. split might add a hop. we need SLOs.
alyssa: We can keep a local read-through cache in enricher-api for prefix/KV with short TTLs. write-through goes to worker async. That keeps p90 stable.
jess: What about consistency? write async means a client may read stale enrichment for a few seconds. acceptable?
omar: For most enrichers it's ok (best-effort). For a subset (fraud checks) we need sync. plan is to mark those as "sync-only" and keep them on the api path until we've rolled out a sync adapter to worker.
mark: Rollout strategy? canary both in Dedicated and Hosted. we should have a fallback route to the monolith for a percentage of traffic.
rachel: Ops checklist: - traffic shaping, - feature flag gate, - migration monitor, - alert on enrichment error rate and p99 latency.
ajess: +1 to alerts. also need eval harness to compare outputs pre/post split to catch regressions.
omar: Good call. We'll wire existing eval sets into the CI job.
infra-bot: Reminder: new service will need IAM roles and mTLS certs in private deploy. create infra ticket.
mark: Data migration details: backfill job should be idempotent, rate-limited, and emit provenance tags so we can roll back. Suggest a migration token per session.
alyssa: Example config for the api facade:
```
ENRICHER_API_CACHE_TTL=3s
ENRICHER_SYNC_LIST=fraud,compliance
ENRICHER_WORKER_QUEUE=projects/prod/topics/enricher-migrate
```
works for me.
jess: Can we include a compatibility sham so old clients continue to call the same endpoint? avoid client changes.
omar: Yes — enricher-api will keep the endpoint surface. internal routing decides worker vs inline.
mark: Metrics to track during rollout: 1) p50/p95/p99 enrichment latency, 2) enrichment error % by enrichertype, 3) KV miss ratio, 4) migration backlog size, 5) canary fallback rate.
rachel: Who owns the cutover? propose: eng-runtime owns the canary automation, eng-platform owns infra, and eng-ml owns the quality gate.
omar: I'll put together an RFC addendum and a cutover runbook. target: start canary next Wed.
alyssa: +1. I'll schedule a 30m sync to validate the runbook.
deploy-bot: Canary started for enricher-api v2 on Dedicated (canary id: canary-88).
mark: saw the canary metrics — initial p95 looks fine but p99 spikes on some enrichers. digging.
jess: If we see p99 regressions, fallback to monolith via routing rule and roll the canary back.
omar: Thanks team. I'll post the RFC addendum link once written.
